Simran Dhaliwal, Senior UX Designer

I’m a Senior UX Designer with 5+ years of experience designing complex enterprise and B2B SaaS products for technical and business users.

My work has spanned AI/ML, cloud and developer tools, APIs, data-heavy workflows, and design systems, mostly at Red Hat. I’ve also worked on community and nonprofit projects and mentored earlier-career designers.

I enjoy getting into unfamiliar problem spaces, connecting the dots, and turning ambiguity into something teams can move forward with.

AI/ML platforms. Model serving. Governance. APIs. Data-heavy workflows. Design systems.

I like problems where there’s more going on underneath the screen than what the user sees.

I want to understand how the system works, where the constraints come from, and how the pieces connect.

The goal isn’t to hide the complexity. It’s to make it understandable, intentional, and manageable.

I have a master’s in computer science (with a focus in Human-Computer Interaction) and an early background in software engineering, so I’m comfortable getting under the hood of a product.

I can follow technical conversations, understand engineering constraints, and build interactive prototypes when static screens aren’t enough.

I’m not trying to be the engineer. I’m comfortable enough with technology to design with engineers and explore what’s possible together.

I use AI to explore ideas, challenge my thinking, learn about unfamiliar areas, build interactive prototypes, and get from concept to something people can experience faster.

I think of AI as a thought partner. It can help me explore possibilities, surface perspectives I may have missed, and expand what I’m able to do.

But generating more isn’t the same as creating more value. The hard part is understanding people, framing the problem, weighing trade-offs, and deciding what’s actually worth building.

That’s where design judgment still matters.

Technology is great. We know how it can help businesses, customers, and people live and work better.

But technology doesn’t exist in a vacuum. If it can help make the world a better place, I believe it also needs to be sustainable.

I try to contribute by volunteering with initiatives that make technology more sustainable or use technology to help solve environmental problems.

I’ve participated in digital sustainability initiatives, environmental education, and citizen-science projects using AI to help researchers identify coral.

Read more in About

Most of my experience has been in enterprise software, but I’m ready to bring that experience into new problem spaces.

I’m interested in roles across enterprise, B2B SaaS, consumer products, healthcare, fintech, developer tools, AI, climate tech, and other domains where the problems are interesting.

I don’t need to already know the domain. I know how to learn it, make sense of it, and design within its constraints.

Case studies

Making AI model access understandable

Platform UXB2B SaaSEnterprise AIShipped

Making AI model access easier to understand, audit, and manage. As more AI models are shared across enterprise teams, administrators need to piece together permissions, usage limits, and model configuration to understand who can use what. I redesigned the governance experience around those relationships, turning fragmented admin views into a single way to understand access, limits, and configuration gaps. The Model view shipped in Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.5.

Designing for Consistency at Scale

Design SystemsB2B SaaSEnterprise AI

I led a design consistency initiative across a 20-designer team, helping break down feature-area silos by making shared patterns and guidance easier to discover, understand, and reuse, so connected experiences could feel seamless across the product.
